text_fidelity_a:
Mainstreet Classics Dutchman 3-in-1 Combo Folding Board Game Set The board is a very nice, stained wood. It measures 15.75" by 15.75" (including the handles) wide by 1" deep when open or 2" when folded. It folds in half, with the recessed backgammon side holding the game pieces during storage. Two pairs of magnets hold the board closed when folded. The magnets have been effective at holding the set closed without being difficult to open when desired. The top board is 8 by 8 squares across. The wood checkers are just under 1" across and have a slight protrusion on the bottom to keep them in place when a piece is crowned. There are 15 pieces each of brown and white, and these pieces are also used for backgammon. The wood chess pieces are common, simple chess shapes and have a felt bottom. The pawns are 1 3/8" tall and the king is 3" tall. The set also includes two wooden cups, two pairs of dice, and a doubling cube for backgammon. The included game instructions are brief and not really enough to learn to play the games, but it's easy enough to find this information online. From the box: "Solid wood travel set accented with walnut, maple, and mahogany playing surfaces" as well as the California Prop 65 warning with "Wash hands after use."

There are some 1 star reviews for this set, and I have a hard time believing it's for the same set. The set I got has lovely workmanship and everything looks sturdy and well-made. The handle is plenty wide (4.25" across and 1" high) and is sanded smooth as well as finished with a stain. There is no obvious glue.
text_fidelity_b: Mainstreet Classics Dutchman 3-in-1 Combo Folding Board Game Set

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Imaginext DC Super Friends, R/C Transforming Batbot Not only do my grand kids love transformer type toys but, my grown children also love them!
This is a great toy when it's in the tank position, then it transforms into a huge robot just by turning the power pad or do it with the remote. I will admit that I didn't do it the "right" way and was shown the proper way of doing it.
It has over 100 phrases and sound effects. Plus it has a remote control to make it move. A childs dream!
I've only stayed around long enough to hear about 15 of them before I left the kids to play.
I especially loved seeing the eyes and the vents lighting up. Of course we had to turn off all the lights to see this bad boy eyes glow in the dark.
To add to the fun, it also comes with small disks that can be launched out in rapid succession. The disks are small and can be a choking hazard so please be careful if using around small children.

It does require 6 AA batteries for the Batbot. 2 AAA batteries for the remote. A LOT of batteries so I'm hoping they last for more than a day.
With this toy I might consider rechargeable batteries depending on how long regular batteries last.

The remote control is in the shape of the "batman" bat. Not only too cute but it fits in the childs hand so nicely.
Also comes with a small batman doll that fits into the belly part of the Batbot.
I am really hoping this toy is made as well as it looks. This is something all the kids will playing with for a very long time.

This transforming Batbot is just too nice of a toy to pass up. A little pricey but, so well worth every cent.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Imaginext DC Super Friends, R/C Transforming Batbot

text_fidelity_a:
Kid Galaxy Remote Control Bump 'n Chuck Bumper Cars. RC Toy Game. 2 Radio Control Vehicles First, let me say that this holds 10 AAA batteries which may turn a lot of people off right from the start. We put all our batteries in and played for a good while until the batteries in the cars died. Luckily, we still had batteries (because we had to buy two packs) to replace the ones in the cars (the ones in the controllers were still good) and they played some more. They travel pretty good distance for a radio controlled car and they are relatively easy to maneuver for young kids. My 5 year old enjoyed playing with them for awhile (and the ferrets were terrified of them! They spent most of the day chasing the dog and ferrets around...which I suppose is entertaining. The little guy flies out of the car when the button on the side is depressed whether by the other car or if it hits against an object. He also yells like he's falling through the air! The bumper cars resemble an airboat to me. The construction is good IMO and its small enough for little hands to handle easily but large enough to see it coming.

The kids enjoyed playing with them for awhile but like most things it gets tossed to the side when something new comes along.

For the cost, there should be more music programmed into it. Over-all, the appeal depends on your child. As for my grandson.... not so much. text_fidelity_a:
Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud This is a completely different kind of game and the idea of stars and lanterns is abstract. It says it is easy to learn, but to be honest, don't bring your friends together to learn the game. You should set it up, read through the directions and pretend to have two friends with you to understand what is going on. THEN you can explain the game to your friends. The reason is because you can tell this game was not designed in America, there are a few minor English mistakes. The directions have interesting choice of words. So I'm going to try my best by using parentheses to show the words they used in the directions.

The goal of the game is when a word card is revealed, you try to figure out which dixit (picture) cards match that word--by the picture itself, the color(s), inspiration, characters, etc. Then you mark an X (cross) for each dixit card you feel matches that word. At the same time, you want to choose cards you think your friends will choose. If your friends chose that card too, both of you earn stars (sparks) and so on. If they didn't, then you lose (fall) and stop there. If you marked X for too many dixit cards (hoping to get a lot of points), more likely your friends won't have that same card marked and that will make you lose. You have to work like a team, trying to figure out what your friends will choose and win. (This is what they mean by the word, greedy.) This is a good way to teach kids how to perceive the pictures and THINK of others and what they could be thinking, again a "teamwork." This is where it is supposed to be fun. My daughter liked it, but my son didn't like it.

I have one suggestion for you as parents or caregiver of a child age 8 or over. (Ages for the game is for 8+.) I suggest you form the first few turns, you handpick the words you feel your child will be able to "match" then go from there. You handpicking and seeing a few cards in advance honestly does not change the game. The game actually entirely relies on the other players' dixit card choices.

There is one rule that seems pointless. Of course you need to read the directions first to understand what I"m talking about. Here I go anyway--suppose you "fall" then at the end of the game when everyone is ready to score. If you have some sparks and a super-spark from one of your dixit cards that you marked off (crosses), you wipe away one star (but not the super-spark star) then count the remaining stars (sparks). The super-spark star has the same point value as the other sparks so I'm not sure why it makes a difference to wipe off a star or a super-spark star.

This game is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. It's also created in China and I don't know that it's going to be that great, at least for some U.S. audiences.
text_fidelity_b: Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud

Crayola Super Tips Markers, Coloring Book Markers, 20 count I was fairly excited when I found these at my local 'more-than-a-dollar' store. I've been working on lettering with markers (Tombows and Copics all the way down to the standard Crayola markers). So here was something I'd never come across in person and I was more than willing to cough up a little cash to try these out.

Unfortunately, my enthusiasm petered out as soon as I opened them. They are definitely manufactured on the cheap and some corners were cut. (Plain white cheap-looking barrel, caps not as secure as any other Crayola marker I've tried.) Still, I hoped for the best and spent several minutes practicing with them.

Sadly, I cannot recommend these whatsoever for 'brush' lettering. I do not understand at all what makes these special, they seem flimsy to me and I'm afraid the tip of the marker will pop right off. I vastly prefer the chubby Crayola markers for lettering and coloring. Save yourself a little money if you're into lettering (or coloring) and move right along.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Super Tips Markers, Coloring Book Markers, 20 count

text_fidelity_a:
BraveRats - A Game by Seiji Kanai After attempting to play this game, I was confused. Honestly, I went to look around at reviews to see what I was missing. I saw such words as “bluffing” and “strategy” and I was left with, “What?!” It seemed like I had a completely different game. It takes a little time to understand everything, though. Without the cheat sheet close by, it was impossible for me to figure out who won. Even then, the “special powers” confused me. The cheat sheet would tell me the winner of a certain combination, but then according to the “special powers”, the other card should have won. (After reading through the instructions again, I saw that the special powers always override the cheat sheet.) I’m embarrassed about my confusion, but I’m throwing it out there in case I can make anybody else out there that’s confused like me feel better.

There are 8 red cards, 8 blue cards, a cheat sheet, and a booklet, all in a tin case. It’s a very quick game. Though it seems like it would be simple, it can be complicated at first. Once you get the hang of it, it is simple, though.

I imagine this will be a perfect game to play with my little ones when they’re a bit older. (My oldest is a delayed 5 right now, but I imagine slightly older children will have fun with this!)

Really, once the initial confusion is dealt with, this is a fun little game!
text_fidelity_b: BraveRats - A Game by Seiji Kanai

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Kindergarten Reading - Learn Spelling & Reading Workbook with Interactive Pen, Ages 5+ Very educational with great building-blocks for reading success. The actual concepts focused in this activity book are great, but there are two areas of improvement outside of the lessons:

The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Kindergarten Reading - Learn Spelling & Reading Workbook with Interactive Pen, Ages 5+

Balloon Arch Kit Adjustable for Different Table Sizes Birthday, Wedding, Christmas, and Graduation Party Update: Second time we used it, one of the plastic clamps broke. I have contacted the seller by phone and by email to purchase JUST the clamps... no response. None. I need to use it for a party next weekend, so I purchased a different one with metal clamps - and having major problems with the new one as well. I would say..... if you need it for a one time use, it's still worth it, but a huge a disappointment that it can't be used again. The balloon stands are still fine.

Original review: I used this arch for my niece's baby shower. I was seriously worried about the stability of the arch, setup, and tear down. But after giving it a test run at my house first, it was so simple to set up and use, and it was very stable. I received a bunch of clips with the set, but I found that putting the balloons around the pole was much easier than using the clips. We also purchased 2 sets of balloon poles, and those were easy to use as well, same method. I took these on a plane across the country, and they traveled well. The only negative, and it is minor, was that there were no instructions included in the boxes. I initially had a hard time getting the poles to stay together, until I YouTubed a Party Zealot setup video, then it became apparent what the glue dots are for! Trust me...you will want to use the glue dots to "glue" the poles together, or they WILL come apart. But using the glue dots made them much more stable. There are still some little blue clippy things that came in the boxes that we never did figure out how to use, and I couldn't find the information anywhere on their website or google searches. So they remain a mystery. But overall, for the money, this was a HUGE success and a fantastic buy. I have never had so many compliments. Highly recommend.

No, the fur doesn't really "shave off" it's more like you comb it off and grab it. It takes parental involvement and it's messy, but it's meant to be an experience, which it fully delivers. The entire experience was magical and bonding for my daughter and I. We giggled and guessed if we would get the Frenchie or Yorkie and wondered what color it's nails would turn. The bath was fun and a bit messy, and blow drying took a while (mostly mom, she got bored) but her favorite part was grooming the Frenchie (it was easy to tell) and adding the little accessories. The surprise factor was 100% on point. The whole time the suspense was palpable for her. She was guessing the whole time and we came up with names for it.
Don't buy this toy if you can't be bothered to spend an hour playing with your child.
Don't buy this toy expecting a 5-7 year old to do this independently.
This toy is clearly meant for interactive play with an adult.
This toy was a wonderful addition to our homeschooling dramatic play for kindergarten.

If you want a toy that allows you and your child to pretend to own a grooming salon, this toy is perfect. Have everything prepared ahead of time. We put a table cloth down and a bowl of warm water with shampoo, then in a separate area we had the drying and grooming station. Expect to spend at least 45-60 minutes on this adorable experience. It's wonderful for people who enjoy playing with their kids. Our whole family loves it.

My four year old is having fun running him around in "line" mode, where his sensors follow a black lined path on a white background. When he reaches the end, he turns around and comes back.

You program multiple commands into the remote, and then you send Botley out on a small adventure, around the obstacle course pieces that you can set up with material from the box. Angry Birds - Sling and Smash Track Set Our kids, ages 3-10, went crazy seeing this Angry Birds- Sling And Smash Track Set. The set couldn't be more easy to set up. It comes with a spring loaded sling shot with a slide to propel Red, the Angry Bird into destroying Pig City. The city has 2 buildings that sit on 4 ladders. You can make the city any way you want and stand the green pig anywhere. There are stickers included to make the buildings look more real. Once set up, all you do, is pull back the spring and Red, who has a wheel base, either flies or rolls into the pig city, knocking it down along with the green pig. The play is simple, but after a while, our kids starting begging for paper towel cardboard tubes, toilet paper tubes, Tupperware, plastic cups, building blocks, anything light and stackable to build pig city taller, wider, bigger and more fun.

They began cutting windows into the paper towel tubes, so the green pig could watch the bird coming. Then they began decorating the tubes, along with our small Ziploc and Tupperware containers. Soon, there was a pig city big enough to play targeting the city all day. I should have known what was coming next. I soon heard begging, that they desperately need more pigs for the city and more birds to attack. So, I found Amazon has extra figures- Angry Birds Movie Mini Figure Multi Pack Set A and a Set B. Each Set includes both birds and pigs- 7 total figures. They are not expensive- around $13.00 for each 7 figure set. So, I bought both sets, and the figures are very cute, making them worth buying just for their cuteness alone. Now, what was a simple fun Red Angry Bird attacking a lone Green Pig in a little 2 building Pig City has turned into 14 more Angry Birds and Pigs living in a Pig City Block designed from cardboard tubes, small Tupperware containers, blocks and wood scraps all designed from our children's imaginations. This simple little Set is a Big 5 STARS.
text_fidelity_b: Angry Birds - Sling and Smash Track Set

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+ We'd already bought the Sneaky Squirrel Game, which is similar to this game. We've though it was one of the cutest games ever, so we were thrilled to add this one to our collection, too!

With this game, you'll get one of the cutest boxes you've ever seen! (Let me note here that the top and bottom of the game box do NOT fit inside each other. It's the same with the squirrel game.) You'll also get a super cute pair of Shelby tweezers, 4 bowls, a packet of bones, and a double spinner.

Playing the game is pretty simple. There can be up to 4 players at a time. Each player will spin first to see if they will get bones or lose bones or just lose a turn. The second spin is to determine how many bones they will win/lose. If they land on a seagull, it means they will lose bones. If they land on the hungry pug, they get to steal bones from another player. Busy pug means they lose a turn, and landing on the bones mean they win bones for their bowl. They can pick up the bones they win/lose with the tweezers.

The tweezers are a great way to develop motor skills. The game itself is a great, fun way to learn counting skills. My 5 year old is delayed and really struggles with numbers, so I'm always thrilled to find a new, exciting way to teach them to him. This is also a fun game for my 2 year old. It IS pretty simple, so I imagine, on average, 2-4, maybe 5, is probably the best ages for this game.

Overall, this is a super cute game! I can highly recommend this AND the Sneaky Squirrel Game for your young little ones!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Math - Preschool Math Workbook to Learn Counting & Colors with Interactive Activities, Classroom Essentials, Ages 3+ We are really loving these Hot Dots learning activity books. My preschooler loves to count, so this math book is great for getting some counting practice in. I never worked on pattern recognition, and this book includes that, so I’m so glad we’re getting some exposure with that (i.e. circle, circle, square, circle, circle —insert what comes next). It also covers big and small, shapes, the most and the least themes, heavy and light, as well as matching. There’s a lot to learn in this workbook, and it’s a lot of fun.

Two areas of improvement: The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Math - Preschool Math Workbook to Learn Counting & Colors with Interactive Activities, Classroom Essentials, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Palace of Mad King Ludwig Palaces of Mad King Ludwig is a tile-laying, castle-building game for two to four players. This game is reminiscent of Carcassonne, except it is a good bit more complicated, requiring players to place building tiles near each other in specific patterns to earn swans of various colors, utilize special powers or scoring rules, and to build both above and below ground while the moat around the castle continually encloses your playspace.

Ultimately, while the components are nice quality, there are quite a lot of bits for a game like this, and the artwork is not particularly interesting. Rooms are largely void of identifiable decoration, making the words easy to read, but the rooms difficult to distinguish. Also of note, in the previous "Mad King" game, a major selling point of the game was mismatched and oddly sized tiles, while this one is entirely composed of squares and rectangles.

All told, we fell like this was a solid game, but one that has just a few too many rules that confine what you can do and what you want to do. Most of the time, there was a clear "best move" available, and rarely were more than, say, three decisions even possible based on what you could buy and where you could place it. I think a lot of people will like this game more than I did, as my fellow players certainly did. I would personally rather play something that is more streamlined (Carcassonne), or simply more interesting (Castles of Mad King Ludwig).

Also of note, Palace of Mad King Ludwig is not related to it's cousin "Castles," which is a little confusing. The idea behind the games is radically different.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Palace of Mad King Ludwig

Moorebot Scout - Tiny AI Camera Robot for Tech-Minded, Pets/Edlerly Watching/Security/Smart Home/Crawlspace Inspection, 1080P, Auto Patrol, Nightvision, Track Option, Indoor (2023) My office was just moved to a new building that as yet has no cameras inside...Well...Sort of. Now I've got Scout here to take care of business. It's like a Ring doorbell on wheels.

I'm having a lot of fun controlling it manually from home. It connects to the wifi at work and I check in on things using the app. It's working very well and seems to hold a signal about 250kbps. 1080p recordings look fine. For myself, the night vision works a charm. It's clear enough to identify people, and that's all that matters. Plus, driving it around my office while I'm in bed is pretty cool, too.

Battery takes about three hours to charge out of the box and it lasts about 2hr running around the building before it goes back to the base. Most recent firmware update makes that process significantly faster, too. If you've got it on a slick surface, it might have some trouble, but it'll get plugged in eventually. Says battery runs out after an hour using only night vision, but you can set that to automatic in the app.

Around the house, the little noises are kinda neat, but for use as security, that'd be something to disable....except the alarm. That's something to keep on in case you need to scare someone off. Recording all that stuff and saving files to the phone is a plus.

I really like this little guy. It's definitely something you'll have to play around with, but it is a load of fun getting set up.

The awesome parental feature is the ability to set a slow speed for littles and increase to 5 mph as they learn better control. text_fidelity_a: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle T. S. Shure had a temporary design lapse with this product; probably, the worst coming out of this brand.  Excellent idea coupled with poor execution only increases the frustration one would feel about the product.  The idea of 'magnetic' pieces to help discover countries and continents is great; so is the use of some cutesy imagery that often is often ascribed to a particular country (the dragon shaped like the Great Wall of China is a clear standout).  But trying to cramp all kinds of information in a tiny board proved disastrous.  The pieces are cut with no logic - the sub-continent looks from another planet; the font size for the capitals is so tiny, the target audience will barely notice it;  there are random airplanes and ships distracting the overall map and adding no value.  The tiny pieces are clearly not to be allowed anywhere near babies (it is rated for 6-15 years, to be fair; though it will be a miracle if anyone in that age group will use this for more than a day).  On the positive, with the weak magnetic pull and cardboard-feeling tiny pieces are bound to be lost sooner or later. And then you could create a new game - "which country is missing?". Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge Simple, serene and elegant, this is a game like few others in your collection. This one is about a trip through Japan, and has very nice Japanese style artwork that really pops. One look at the box cover will tell you how elegant and evocative this game is, and that really is one of it's finest features.

Gameplay is rather simple. Those who rush ahead to see the sights first certainly get some kind of advantage - they often get first choice of where to go - while those who take their time will have plenty of opportunity to catch up, as the last player is always the next to move, meaning that travellers who venture too far out will allow others to make every stop along the way. There are "safe" and predictable options where you always get two or three points, and there are gambling options where you might be able to buy cards that give you far more.

It's a good, simple game that works well as a gateway game, but like many games, it says it's a decent two-player game, and I don't think that it is. It shines with three to four players. The decisions are not particularly deep or exciting, and much of the time, there really are only two choices that you can choose from - move really slow, or move really fast - and those choices are often easy to make.

If you're a gamer, I don't think you'll like this game. You can find better gateway games for sure, and there are thousands of games where you'll make more interesting choices. If you're just getting into games, or if you need something new to play with grandma, then this might be the best choice you can make.
text_fidelity_b: Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge

Melissa & Doug Deluxe Wooden Magnetic Responsibility Chart With 90 Magnets This is an ok chart but with some issues. I really really wanted to love it because I've never been disappointed with Melissa & Doug products. For those wondering, it has the exact same tasks and pictures as the other Melissa & Doug Responsibility chart. It just does not have a spot for the child's name.

The good:
It's got a decent selection of tasks that. The visuals are great and easy to understand for my non-reader. The reward smileys are fun to pick out and have a rainbow selection of colors. It can easily hang (though it's a bit heavy).

The bad:
My board was warped, so the magnets don't fully stick. In addition, it was shipped with a plastic covering over the white boards. Unfortunately the magnets stuck to this plastic and peeled plastic off when trying to use it. This makes the magnets less sticky (see picture for example). This happened to more magnets than were good ones. There are only 26 choices of tasks, which make it pretty minimal. They are geared toward much younger kids, so my five year old won't use most of the magnets as he's already consistently doing these things. I wish there was a larger selection as the children age. There's not enough room for all of the extra magnets to be stored on the bottom half when not in use. One task does not fit if you have all of the smileys and all of the excess tasks down below.

Overall, I'm happy with the product but sure wish it didn't arrive with the above stated damage.

The fact is, this is one of the more simplistic Technic kits we've tried, and that makes this Technic set a good one for those who have never built with this style of blocks before. These are more "Engineer-y" than the standard sets, and will teach simple mechanical principles as you build the pull-motion propulsion system from scratch, and kids can see how it comes together.

If regular LEGO is a teaching toy, this is even better.

That said, Technic is harder to be creative with, so these blocks don't get a lot of play with the standard set once the fun of the kit wears away. My daughter had a little trouble building this, but she is on the younger edge of the age range, so Dad had to do a number of the trickier steps.
